represents: The commanded state of exactly three signals the monitored block consumes - the hopper high-level sensor, the FORWARD shredder running feedback, and the shared operator fault reset - injected at the input map's test members and at DB_Controls.FaultReset, with the REVERSE feedback's test member held clear alongside them (FB_HopperBlockageStim N21, N22; FC_Inputs N1 lines for Test[5]/Test[6]/Test[8]; FC_ControlMain N8 lines 91-93). N23 and N24 write only the block's own statics; nothing else in the block writes outside its own instance.

Presentation of that commanded state to the monitored block within the SAME scan it is computed: the model is called from Main N1, ahead of the input map (Main N2) and the control (Main N3), and the monitored block is itself called at FC_ControlMain N9 inside that third call. The model is called from no other block.

Six timeline shapes selected by the TENS digit of Profile (N7 DIV by 10), with segment boundaries accumulated from the commanded P1..P4 (N8, recomputed from scratch each scan so there is no accumulation drift): shape 1 hopper high and plant running throughout; shape 2 hopper high with the plant never running; shape 3 plant running throughout with the hopper low for [T1,T2); shape 4 hopper high throughout with the plant stopped for [T1,T2); shape 5 plant stopped for [T1,T4) with the hopper low for [T2,T3), i.e. the clear falls wholly inside the stop; shape 6 neither signal driven, hopper low and plant stopped (N11, N12, N13, N14).

A hopper clear of any commanded duration of one CPU scan or longer - including one deliberately SHORTER than the monitored block's clear-debounce filter time - as a stimulus, by choosing P2 (shape 3) or P3 (shape 5) (N8, N11).

A commanded operator reset in four modes (N16, N17): never asserted inside the scenario; one pulse of ResetPulseWidth = T#500MS at ScenarioT = ResetAt; continuously true for the whole scenario phase; one pulse of the same width at the model's own ModelThreshold value.

A fixed LEADING clear-down of T#5S before the scenario, in which the hopper is driven LOW and the plant driven STOPPED, containing a commanded reset asserted from T#3S to T#4S of the run (N4, N5, N9 InCleardown, N16 ClearDownReset, reaching the plant via N17 and N21). This is a statement about what the model DRIVES, not about the state the monitored block ends up in.

A run that begins with NO leading clear-down at all - Offset = T#0S and InCleardown never true - whenever the retentive PreBoundaryDone is already set when the run latches (N5, N9). This is the form a run takes after an externally performed CPU stop/restart.

A pre-boundary conditioning interval in which the hopper is high AND the plant is running for the commanded PreBoundaryHighRunning, entered only when Precondition = 1 and PreBoundaryDone is clear (N9 InPreBoundary, N13, N14), ending in the latching of a single retentive Bool (N10). That Bool is the entire boundary mechanism the block contains.
A published observation window, Stim.Armed, true only while the scenario phase is running and only for ScenarioT in [ArmAt, ArmUntil) (N18), for arming observation latches outside this block.

A published, latched completion flag, Stim.ScenarioDone, set at ScenarioT >= EndAt (N19), which also drops the run latch on the following scan (N1) and thereby leaves the hopper low and the plant stopped; it is re-armed only after the harness drops Start (N20).

A run that cannot be truncated by the harness dropping Start part-way through: Running seals itself and is broken only by ScenarioDone (N1). The scenario runs to EndAt, the reset pulses still fire, and injection stays engaged.

Restoration of the field OUTSIDE a run, in two DISJOINT windows - and specifically NOT at the moment a run ends. Test[0] is Running OR InTrailingCleardown (N21) and InTrailingCleardown requires NOT Stim.Start (N24), so the field is connected (a) from the scan after ScenarioDone latches until the harness drops Start - an UNBOUNDED window, during which the harness is reading the result and FC_Inputs takes Hopper_Level_High and Shredder_Run_Fwd_FB from DI8_HPR_LevelHigh and DI5_SHR_RunFwdFB again - and (b) after the trailing clear-down completes and TrailingTimer.Q clears CleardownPending (N23). Injection is re-engaged in between. Whether window (a) is material depends on what those terminals read on the rig, which no reading of the IR establishes.

A TRAILING clear-down after the harness acknowledges a result. When a run reaches ScenarioDone, N23 latches CleardownPending; when the harness then drops Start, N24 runs TrailingTimer for ClearDownTime = T#5S and drives, for that duration: Test[0] high (N21), Test[6] held clear (N22), Test[5] and Test[8] low (both ANDed with Running, which is false), and TrailingReset true across TrailingT in [T#3S, T#4S), which N21 puts onto DB_Controls.FaultReset. TrailingTimer.Q then clears CleardownPending (N23). Stated as what the model DRIVES, not as the state the monitored block ends up in.
doesNotRepresent: Any physical or process behaviour of a hopper. There is no material, no level dynamics, no in-flight mass, no sensor noise and no coupling whatsoever between the plant-running signal and the hopper-level signal: both are computed from Shape and elapsed time alone (N13, N14). Shape 2 holds the hopper high with the plant stopped indefinitely and nothing in the block forbids a physically impossible combination.

An equipment-grounded model in the sense of spec S11 M2. The six shapes were fitted to the CASES THE SPECIFICATION AND VECTOR SET ASK FOR - the block's own comment still says so ('six shapes cover every scenario the vector set asks for') - so the model inherits the register's assumptions and the register's blind spots are not represented by construction.

The field-side signal path. Values are injected at the input buffer's test members (N21), so DI5_SHR_RunFwdFB and DI8_HPR_LevelHigh are bypassed entirely while Test[0] is high (FC_Inputs N1). No wire break, stuck-at, contact bounce, DI hardware input filtering or terminal polarity is represented. Note also that the map's test branch is 'OR AlwaysTrue AND Test[n]' and does NOT include Test[0]: a set Test[n] injects even with the test flag low. That does not bite for this model, whose Test[5]/Test[8] are ANDed with Running, but the flag is not the gate N21's comment describes.

The REVERSE running feedback, or the plant-running condition as an OR of two directions. The model drives the forward feedback only and force-clears the reverse feedback's test member for the whole run AND for the trailing clear-down (N22), while the monitored block's PlantRunning is Fwd OR Rev (FC_ControlMain line 92).

A coherent plant input image. DB_Input.Test[0] is the input map's SINGLE GLOBAL test-enable and there are 22 such rungs in FC_Inputs consuming Test[1]..Test[22]. The model drives three. The other NINETEEN are written by nothing in the corpus, hold their Bool default, and are forced FALSE for the duration regardless of the field: Control_Healthy, SpareDI[1], Cycle_Start, Cycle_Stop, Motor_Fault, Infeed_Conv_Running, Discharge_Conv_Running, Pusher_PowerPack_Running, Pusher_Home_Limit, Pusher_Full_Travel_Limit, Pusher_High_Pressure, Downstream_Running, Pusher_Local_Remote, SpareDI[2..7]. The model does not model those inputs; it suppresses them. Two consequences: Cycle_Stop INVERTS, because the map negates the terminal (NOT DI4_SYS_CycleStop) but does not negate the test branch, so in test mode it reads false = 'not commanding stop', the opposite of the fail-safe reading of an unwired NC button; and the suppression reaches a terminal, because DB_Output.In_Cycle (FC_ControlMain line 83) is an OR of five of these forced members and drives DQ8_SYS_InCycle.

A reset private to the monitored block, or one confined to a run. N21's fourth rung is a PLAIN COIL with no enable - DB_Controls.FaultReset := TrailingReset OR Running AND Stim.FaultReset - evaluated EVERY SCAN IN EVERY STATE, including idle, where it writes false. A repo-wide grep finds NO OTHER WRITER of DB_Controls.FaultReset anywhere in the PLC program, because it is the HMI operator command surface (DB_Controls.ir, C-306). The model runs at Main N1 and all five consumers are in FC_ControlMain at Main N3: the shredder sequencer (line 23), the motor system (line 39), the pusher (line 59), DB_Output.Motor_Fault_Reset (line 84) and the monitored block (line 93). So an operator/HMI/Modbus/watch-table write to DB_Controls.FaultReset is DESTROYED BEFORE ANY CONSUMER READS IT for as long as this block is in the cyclic program; every commanded pulse also resets the sequencer, the motor FB and the pusher FB; and DB_Output.Motor_Fault_Reset reaches DQ11_SHR_FaultReset (FC_Outputs line 25), so EVERY RESET PULSE ENERGISES A PHYSICAL RELAY OUTPUT. The block's own header still says it 'writes no plant tag'; that sentence survived the edit that produced the current version.

A CPU stop, a CPU restart, or a power cycle. The block cannot command, cause, detect or confirm one. Nothing in it records that a restart occurred; the only thing it carries across is the single retentive Bool PreBoundaryDone (N10), which is set BEFORE any restart and says only that the pre-boundary phase completed. OB100.ir names neither this model's iDB, nor the monitored block's, nor DB_Input.Test[], nor DB_Controls.FaultReset - correct for the design, but it means there is no startup evidence to read.

A HELD pre-boundary wait for that restart - CONTRADICTS THE BLOCK'S OWN COMMENTS. InPreBoundaryWait requires NOT PreBoundaryDone (N9) and N10 sets PreBoundaryDone from InPreBoundaryWait, so the wait state is true for EXACTLY ONE SCAN (~25 ms on the program that runs today) and can never be waited in. On the next scan Offset flips from ClearDownTime to T#0S (N5), so ScenarioT jumps forward by 5 s (N6), and either (a) EndAt <= PreBoundaryHighRunning + 5 s, in which case N19 latches ScenarioDone immediately and N20 RESETS THE RETAINED PreBoundaryDone in the same scan - the boundary marker is destroyed and the run ends - or (b) EndAt is larger, in which case the model resumes driving the scenario from a clock already 5 s + PreBoundaryHighRunning into a timeline whose segments T1..T4 are measured from zero. The model has no mechanism to zero its own scenario clock at the boundary; only the CPU restart, which clears the non-retentive Running and RunTimer, can do that. Related and recorded rather than resolved: even with NO restart, the InPreBoundaryWait -> InScenario transition does not re-zero ScenarioT, so a Precondition = 1 scenario begins at ScenarioT ~ PreBoundaryHighRunning and P1, ArmAt, ResetAt and EndAt all INCLUDE the pre-boundary duration. The UDT's own wording supports that reading; this declaration does not license the opposite one.

A boundary-aware suppression of the TRAILING clear-down - CONTRADICTS N23'S OWN COMMENT. N23 is SCOIL CleardownPending := Stim.ScenarioDone AND NOT PreBoundaryDone, and its comment calls the second term 'the whole protection for the startup scenarios'. But N20, four networks earlier in the same scan, is RCOIL PreBoundaryDone := Stim.ScenarioDone. So in the scan N19 latches ScenarioDone, N20 clears PreBoundaryDone and N23 evaluates NOT PreBoundaryDone as TRUE UNCONDITIONALLY; it cannot recover, because PreBoundaryDone is set only by N10 from InPreBoundaryWait, which requires Running, which N1 holds false while ScenarioDone is latched. THE TERM IS PROVABLY DEAD. The behaviour the comment describes is still delivered - across an externally performed stop/restart ScenarioDone is false, so nothing is owed - so this declaration CLAIMS THE BEHAVIOUR AND DOES NOT CLAIM THE MECHANISM. Anything citing NOT PreBoundaryDone as the reason is citing a term that contributes nothing.

The monitored block's persistence threshold, or the instant it crosses it. ModelThreshold is a stimulus constant held as the instance start value T#60S (iDB_HopperBlockageStim line 23) and is never read from the monitored block; ResetMode 3 places its pulse at the model's own number (N15, N16). It currently agrees with iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor.IO.BlockedTimeThreshold = T#60S BY COINCIDENCE OF TWO INDEPENDENTLY HAND-SET START VALUES, with no check anywhere in the corpus. Retune the monitored block and ResetMode 3 fires at the wrong instant, silently.

Any observation, expectation or judgement of the monitored block. No network of this block reads any member of iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor; Armed and ScenarioDone are published, never compared against anything.

ANY BOUNDARY-OBSERVABLE RECORD OF THE STIMULUS ITSELF. FC_HarnessCopyLayer N7/N8 publishes the monitored block's HopperBlockedAlarm (HX_HBA_R000) and HopperBlockStopReq (R001), the model's Armed (R002) and ScenarioDone (R003), four violation latches (R004-R007) and two phase-armed response latches (L008/L009). Stim.Hopper, Stim.Run and Stim.FaultReset are mirrored NOWHERE, and Stim.Hopper/Stim.Run are read by no block outside this one at all. A harness cannot confirm from the boundary that the hopper was actually driven high - only that the model believed it was in the armed part of a scenario. The stimulus is UNWITNESSED; only its phase and the block-under-test's response are witnessed. Related timing fact: ScenarioDone is cleared by N20 in the same scan Start falls, and L008/L009 are reset by the copy layer on NOT HX_HBA_Start in that same scan, so R003, L008 and L009 are readable ONLY while Start is high.

The state the monitored block is actually in when a scenario starts. Both clear-downs drive the hopper low for 5 s and pulse the shared reset; whether that leaves the block unalarmed with a zeroed accumulator is the BLOCK'S behaviour, and this model neither establishes nor verifies it - for the leading clear-down or the trailing one. Note also that the coupling N4's comment relies on - T#5S being longer than the monitored block's ClearDebounceTime (T#2S) - is UNENFORCED: nothing links the two numbers, and raising ClearDebounceTime above T#3S would put the reset pulse before the filter expires, silently.

Sub-scan timing, and one scan on THIS program is ~2.26 ms. Every phase boundary is a comparison against the run timer's ET sampled once per OB1 scan (N2, N3), so commanded transitions land on scan boundaries and two commanded transitions less than one scan apart collapse into one. The narrowest reset the model can command is T#500MS inside the scenario (N4 ResetPulseWidth) and 1 s inside either clear-down (N4 ClearResetFrom/ClearResetUntil) - so a scenario reset pulse is ~221 scans wide and a clear-down pulse ~442. THE FIGURE WITH ITS PROVENANCE, BECAUSE THE PROVENANCE IS THE WHOLE POINT: the program deployed on this rig - GenProject1, stamp 16#41E5DA59 - measures ~2.26 ms/scan, measured directly off the rig as scan-counter deltas against wall clock, three times: 2.2629 ms (79.906 s / 35,312 scans), 2.2733 ms, and 2.2041 ms (fastest observed). This is a property of THAT program and does not transfer, which is exactly the error this entry has now been wrong about TWICE. (a) The first declaration quoted ~2.1 ms sourced to CLAUDE.md; that belongs to a BARE HARNESS program deployed 2026-08-14 and not on the rig since, so it was approximately right by accident and wrong by provenance. (b) This declarer then replaced it with 23.80 / 24.931 ms from src/harness/Harness.Wire/WireTiming.cs; that is a faithful record of the JOB9004 PLANT + HARNESS program, which is NOT what is on this rig, so it was wrong by an order of magnitude in the opposite direction. Corrected here. docs/notes/live-project-readiness.md states the rule both errors broke - 'Every row in this table is a property of the PROGRAM, not of the controller' - and THAT TABLE CURRENTLY CARRIES NO ROW FOR GenProject1 AS DEPLOYED; the three figures above are recorded here and are not yet in it. Do not quote any of them without the program they were measured against. WHAT THIS MOVES: it makes the sub-scan floor ~11x FINER than this declarer previously wrote, so this limitation is weaker rather than stronger, and every conclusion elsewhere in this document survives it unchanged. The one derived bound that consumes the scan is the timer floor, EffectiveTimerFloor = max(500 ms, k * scan) with k ~ 5 (TimeCompression.cs): at 2.26 ms the scan term is ~11 ms, so the ABSOLUTE 500 ms floor binds - as it also did at 24.9 ms (~125 ms). That conclusion is insensitive to which figure is right, and k ~ 5 is X-D's own number and has never been measured.

Runs longer than the run timer. RunTimer's PT is the LITERAL T#10M (N2) - not an interface member, so the harness cannot change it - and a TON's ET stops at PT, so RunT saturates at ten minutes and every phase comparison freezes with it: a run whose clear-down plus EndAt exceeds that never reaches EndAt, never publishes ScenarioDone, never ends, and leaves Test[0] high indefinitely. RunTimer.Q, the one signal that would detect this, is read NOWHERE in the block.

Validation of the commanded vector. Shape is Profile / 10 (N7); any Profile whose tens digit is not 1..5 - including 0, 6 and 7 or above - drives nothing at all and is indistinguishable in the driven signals from the deliberate idle shape 6. An unset or out-of-range command is a silent idle run, never a refusal. The defaults compound: ArmAt = ArmUntil = T#0S means Armed (N18) is NEVER true, so a defaulted run completes having observed nothing and publishes ScenarioDone in doing so.

More than one hopper clear or more than one plant stop per run. Each shape yields at most one clear interval and at most one stop interval (N11, N12), so a second high episode after a re-accumulation, a second clear, or repeated stop/start within one scenario is not representable in a single run.

An observation window that outlasts the scenario. Armed is ANDed with InScenario (N18), so an ArmUntil beyond EndAt is silently truncated at EndAt, and no ArmAt/ArmUntil window can open during the clear-down or the pre-boundary phase.

A run containing no operator reset at all, OR a ResetMode 2 run presenting a single rising edge. Every run that starts with a leading clear-down asserts the commanded reset from 3 s to 4 s of the run irrespective of ResetMode (N16, N17); ResetMode 0 means 'no reset inside the scenario', not 'no reset in this run'. CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS DECLARATION, which said ResetMode 2 presents exactly ONE rising edge 'with nothing after it': the trailing clear-down falsifies the second half. On the plant reset (DB_Controls.FaultReset, N21) a ResetMode 2 run now goes true 3-4 s, false 4-5 s, true from the scenario's first scan to ScenarioDone, false through the whole unbounded window in which the harness still holds Start, then TRUE AGAIN for 3-4 s into the trailing clear-down - TWO rising edges, the second after the result was read, delivered plant-wide. Note also that Stim.FaultReset, which FB_HarnessViolationLatch watches (N1-N3), does NOT carry the trailing pulse: N17 is unchanged and only N21 ORs in TrailingReset. The violation instrument and the monitored block therefore watch two different reset signals, identical during a run and divergent after it.

A scenario latched at the start of a run. FC_HarnessCopyLayer N3-N5 copies the vector registers into the model's iDB with UNCONDITIONAL MOVEs every scan, so a client that rewrites EndAt, P1..P4, ArmAt, ResetMode or Profile mid-run changes the RUNNING scenario, with one scan of latency and no record that it happened. The model represents a scenario as commanded at each scan, not as commanded at T=0.

A guaranteed trailing clear-down. InTrailingCleardown (N24) requires NOT Stim.Start, so if the harness re-raises Start inside the phase it goes false immediately, TrailingTimer resets, and CleardownPending STAYS LATCHED - only TrailingTimer.Q clears it (N23). The phase can therefore run for a partial duration or ZERO TIMES, with CleardownPending persisting into the next run and being re-set at its end. N23's comment says the phase 'runs once per completed run'; it can run zero times. The next run's LEADING clear-down covers the hygiene, so the outcome is benign, but 'every completed run is followed by a full 5 s clear-down' is not a claim this model supports.

THE BLOCK'S OWN HEADER CONTAINS A FALSE SENTENCE ABOUT ITS PLANT WRITES, AND IT IS THE SENTENCE A READER WOULD RELY ON INSTEAD OF CHECKING. The block COMMENT says the model 'writes no plant tag'. It writes DB_Controls.FaultReset - the plant's ONLY operator-reset surface, the HMI command surface named as such in DB_Controls.ir - unconditionally, every scan, in every state (N21, a plain coil with no enable), as the SOLE PLC writer, reaching five consumers including the monitored block and the physical relay output DQ11_SHR_FaultReset. Every clause of the header sentence is false, and that sentence SURVIVED THE VERY EDIT THAT PRODUCED THE CURRENT VERSION of this block - the edit that added a SECOND write of the same tag (N23/N24 -> TrailingReset -> N21). Recorded as a fidelity entry rather than filed as a code defect because of its effect on evidence: an undocumented behaviour prompts a reader to go and check, whereas a false header sentence ANSWERS the question so the reader does not. Anyone auditing this model's blast radius by reading it - the M5 review the spec requires, precisely because a wrong model silently corrupts every vector that uses it - is told in the block's own voice that the blast radius is zero. NO ASSERTION, REVIEW FINDING OR RESULT MAY REST ON THAT SENTENCE, and this declaration contradicts it outright. Correcting the comment is a lad-coder matter and is not done here.
_loadBearingLimitation: READ BEFORE THE LISTS; IT CONDITIONS EVERY ENTRY IN THEM. Two facts compose and together bound what ANY assertion resting on this model can mean. (1) THE STIMULUS IS NOT OBSERVABLE - AT ALL, ANYWHERE. Stim.Hopper, Stim.Run and Stim.FaultReset reach NO mirror register, and Stim.Hopper/Stim.Run are read by no block outside this one. FC_HarnessCopyLayer publishes the model's PHASE (Armed, ScenarioDone) and the block-under-test's RESPONSE, and nothing of what was applied. A wave can confirm the model believed it was in the armed part of a scenario and can see how the monitored block responded; it can NEVER witness that the hopper was actually driven high. See doesNotRepresent entry 12. (2) THERE IS NO COMMITTED SimaticML EXPORT OF THIS MODEL TO CHECK THE IR AGAINST. simatic-ml/test-project001/ holds 26 files and none is FB_HopperBlockageStim, UDT_HopperBlockageStim or iDB_HopperBlockageStim, so converter drift-check has nothing to compare; drift between the object this document describes and the object in the controller can be neither confirmed nor excluded. See _corpusIntegrity. COMPOSED: every claim in this document is an inference from IR that cannot be shown to describe the running object, about a stimulus that is never observed. A PASS against this model means 'the monitored block behaved as expected, GIVEN WHAT WE BELIEVE WAS APPLIED TO IT', and the belief is instrumented nowhere. Per the test-environment contract a declaration describing a drifted object makes every M4 pass a set-difference against the wrong set, and the verdict for that is STALE - never FAIL, never REFUSED - because neither the block nor the vector author would have done anything wrong. THE CHEAPEST REPAIR IS (1): mirror the three driven booleans. They are already Bool statics in an iDB the copy layer writes every scan, and three spare bits would convert this document's central weakness from an unfalsifiable inference into an observation. Noted, not proposed - that is a lad-coder matter and a change to the thing under test.
_declaredBy: SECOND, INDEPENDENT DECLARATION - a re-derivation, not an edit. The block changed after the first declaration (two networks appended, N21/N22 changed in place; see _changeSinceLastDeclaration) and the first declaration no longer described it. Every entry above, including carried-over ones, was re-verified against the current IR and cited to a network in it. Derived by an agent that did not read, and has not read, any conformance vector file, the assertion enumeration, any wave result, the submission document or its model object, or agent-tasks/hopper-wave-deploy/; and that was deliberately NOT told what the block author changed, deriving the change from the IR and from git diff of the .ir files alone. Per CLAUDE.md hard rule 8 the IR was read by a lad-reader sub-agent - neither the block author nor any vector author - held to the same embargo and confirming compliance; the judgement is the declarer's. Sources: ir/test-project001/FB_HopperBlockageStim.ir, UDT_HopperBlockageStim.ir, iDB_HopperBlockageStim.ir, and for the delivery path FC_Inputs.ir, FC_Outputs.ir, FC_ControlMain.ir, DB_Input.ir, DB_Controls.ir, Main.ir, OB100.ir, FC_HarnessCopyLayer.ir, FB_HarnessViolationLatch.ir, HarnessMirror.ir, FB_HopperBlockageMonitor.ir, iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor.ir, UDT_HopperBlockageIO.ir. The register (gen/test-project001/hopper-blockage-alarm/requirements.md) was read for VOCABULARY only; no entry above is justified by it. NOTE ON IDENTITY: the declaredBy value is LEFT UNCHANGED because the submission resolves against it, but this document was NOT written by the agent that wrote the first one. A distinct id (e.g. model-fidelity-declarer-2) is the correct bookkeeping and is raised for decision rather than applied silently, because changing it requires the submission's model reference to be updated in the same act.
_changeSinceLastDeclaration: Derived from git diff HEAD; the change is UNCOMMITTED in the working tree (+27 -6), and converter digest reports 24 networks where the first declaration described 22. Appended: N23 'Trailing Clear-Down Pending' and N24 'Trailing Clear-Down Window', plus five new non-retentive statics (CleardownPending, InTrailingCleardown, TrailingReset, TrailingT, TrailingTimer). Changed in place: N21 Test[0] := Running became Running OR InTrailingCleardown, and DB_Controls.FaultReset := Running AND Stim.FaultReset became TrailingReset OR Running AND Stim.FaultReset; N22 RCOIL Test[6] := Running became Running OR InTrailingCleardown. N1-N20 were NOT renumbered and NOT edited, in this change or the one before it, so a citation to N1-N20 by number remains sound while a citation to N21/N22 has the right number and the wrong rung. No UDT member and no iDB start value changed. TWO ENTRIES OF THE FIRST DECLARATION ARE FALSIFIED BY THIS CHANGE and are corrected above: represents 12 (field restored at the end of a run) and doesNotRepresent 17 as it then stood (ResetMode 2 presents one rising edge with nothing after it). One further entry was stale for an unrelated reason: the previous doesNotRepresent 12 quoted a scan time since retracted.
_validatedAgainstPlantData: FALSE, re-declared, and the absence is recorded per spec S11 M5. No plant observation of any kind exists for this model in this repository - no level trace, no blockage event log, no sensor chatter statistics - and the target is a bench rig whose outputs are physically incapable of actuating. The model's timeline shapes are derived from the specification's cases, not from equipment behaviour (see the S11 M2 entry in doesNotRepresent). Nothing in the current block moves this flag; no reading of a block can establish comparison against real plant data.
_scanTimeBudget: NOT DECLARED - a gap, stated rather than filled, and now TWO gaps. (1) SCAN-TIME BUDGET: spec S11 M3 requires one alongside the represents/doesNotRepresent lists, and no measurement of this block in isolation exists. It is a single FB called once from Main N1, now 24 LAD networks (was 22) with TWO TONs (was one), 35 statics, no loops and no block calls. The only measured figure is whole-program: ~2.26 ms/scan for GenProject1 (stamp 16#41E5DA59), the program actually deployed on this rig, which includes this block but does not attribute it. NEITHER of the two figures previously written into this document applies - not the ~2.1 ms of the first declaration (a bare harness program) nor the 23.80/24.931 ms this declarer wrote (the JOB9004 plant+harness program); see doesNotRepresent entry 14 for the provenance of all three. The budget cannot be inferred from the whole-program figure, and the change since the first declaration added a second TON and two networks, so even a prior per-block measurement would now be stale. (2) compStable: ABSENT. Per docs/notes/test-environment-contract.md section 2.3 this is reported and does not gate at runtimeCompression = 1, and is a REFUSAL at any applied factor above 1x. It is not supplied because no reading of the block establishes at what compression the model still behaves as declared, and inventing a number is exactly the unfounded input the contract refuses rather than defaults. Any wave wanting to run this model compressed must obtain it by measurement, not from this document.
_notComputable: What DI5_SHR_RunFwdFB and DI8_HPR_LevelHigh read on the rig. This decides whether represents 12's first release window - injection off, field connected, while the harness is reading the result - is cosmetic or material. If those terminals are unterminated-low the effect is nil; if either can be high, the monitored block resumes accruing on the real field during the read. Terminal state is not expressible in IR. This is the single fact this declarer would most want confirmed against the rig wiring.

Whether the harness command mirror survives a CPU stop/restart. Stim.Start comes from HX_HBA_Start at %M1009.0 and the vector registers from %MW1012 upward (HarnessMirror.ir, via FC_HarnessCopyLayer N3-N5). Marker retentivity is a CPU hardware-configuration property expressed in no IR file, so whether a post-restart run can re-latch Running - and with what commanded durations - is not decidable from the corpus. Recorded as unknown rather than resolved. Re-verified: still not expressible in the IR.

Whether DB_Input.Test[] and DB_Output.Test[] are retentive. Not declared in the IR. It does not affect Test[0]/Test[5]/Test[8] - the model rewrites all three unconditionally at Main N1 before FC_Inputs runs, so a stale value survives zero scans - and Test[6] is only ever reset. Recorded for completeness.
_corpusIntegrity: iDB_HopperBlockageStim.ir carries 21 of the FB's 35 statics.
